raw_text:
Goal: Maintain current muscle mass and strength during 2 weeks of hotel-room-only training (yoga mat + door pull-up bar). Priority is to preserve hypertrophy and neuromuscular strength, manage fatigue while keeping volume and intensity enough to avoid losses. Program assumes intermediate lifter, available bodyweight, unilateral, tempo and density strategies, and optional slow eccentrics, pauses, and partials to increase stimulus. No equipment—use door pull-up bar for pulling, single-leg/split variations, elevated feet, backpack with clothes as light load if available (optional). Calorie intake should be maintenance; protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight if possible.

General guidelines
- Frequency: 4 sessions/week (upper/lower/upper/lower) — fits travel schedule while allowing recovery.
- Session length: 30–45 minutes.
- Rep ranges: Hypertrophy-maintenance focus: 6–20 reps depending on exercise. Use slower eccentrics (3–4 s) and paused or isometric holds to increase time under tension when load is limited.
- Intensity: Strive for sets that reach near-failure on 1–3 working sets per exercise. Because external load is limited, use variations (e.g., single-leg, elevated-feet push-ups, assisted/unassisted one-arm rows on bar, negative-focused pull-ups) to make exercises challenging.
- Volume: Aim for 10–18 working sets for each major muscle group each week. With 4 sessions, that’s about 2–5 sets per muscle group per session.
- Progression: Increase difficulty via tempo, pause, range-of-motion, unilateral work, or increasing reps/sets. For pull-ups, use negatives, holds, and band alternatives if available (use towel looped over bar for isometric rows if needed).
- Recovery: Sleep 7–9 h/night if possible. Keep mobility short daily (5–10 min), foam rolling or self-massage if possible. Walk 20–40 min on rest days to support recovery and keep calories balanced.
- Nutrition: Maintain maintenance calories; small deficit may cause loss, surplus may gain (not desired). Protein 1.8–2.2 g/kg bodyweight, spread across meals. Carbs around workouts. Stay hydrated.

Equipment hacks (optional)
- Backpack filled with clothes or books for added load for rows, split squats, or press variations.
- Use a towel looped over the pull-up bar for bodyweight “inverted” rows if a safe anchor is available.
- Use door frame for RNT single-arm pushing (careful—only use manufacturer-recommended anchor points).

Two-week program overview
Week 1: Familiarization with hotel variations, slightly higher intensity (near failure) to preserve neuromuscular stimulus.
Week 2: Maintain intensity, slightly higher density (shorter rest) to sustain stimulus despite lower load.

Session structure (each session)
- Warm-up (5–7 min): dynamic mobility, bandless shoulder/hip prep, 1–2 light movement sets.
- Main work: 3–5 exercises, 2–4 working sets each, near-failure on last set; rest 60–120 s depending on goal and exercise complexity.
- Finishers/core: 1–2 short circuits or core sets.
- Cool-down: 3–5 min stretching or breathing.

Detailed plan

Week 1

Day 1 — Upper A (pull emphasis)
Warm-up: shoulder circles, bandless scapular pull-ups (3 × 8 scapular retractions), 2 ramp sets of push-ups (8–12).
1) Pull-ups (use full pull-up if can): 4 sets × 3–8 reps OR if unable: 4 sets of 4–6 reps negatives/slow eccentrics (5–6 s down), or 6–10 reps Australian (inverted) rows using towel/door frame. Rest 90–120 s.
2) Archer/Uneven Pull Variation or Commando Rows on bar (one side emphasis): 3 sets × 6–10 reps each side (or 6–10 reps total if using rows). Slow eccentric 3 s. Rest 90 s.
3) Elevated-feet push-ups (feet on bed/chair): 3 sets × 8–15 reps (add pause at bottom 1–2 s on harder sets). Rest 60–90 s.
4) Pike push-ups or decline pike (for shoulder pressing): 3 sets × 6–12 reps. Rest 90 s.
Finisher/core:
- Dead-bug or hollow holds: 3 × 30–45 s total tension.
- Optional metabolic finisher: 3 rounds EMOM (every minute on minute) of 8–12 mountain climbers + 6 diamond push-ups (not to failure), or 6–8′ of high-intensity interval (30 s on /30 s off) for conditioning.

Day 2 — Lower A (quad/glute focus)
Warm-up: bodyweight squats, leg swings, hip circles.
1) Bulgarian split squats (rear foot on bed/chair): 4 sets × 8–15 reps per leg. If too easy, increase tempo (3 s down), pause at depth 2 s, or hold a backpack for load. Rest 90–120 s.
2) Single-leg Romanian deadlift (bodyweight or backpack): 3 sets × 8–12 reps per leg; focus on slow eccentric and hip hinge. Rest 90 s.
3) Narrow/slow tempo squat (to a chair or deep bodyweight squat): 3 sets × 12–20 reps, 3–4 s eccentric. Rest 60–90 s.
4) Glute bridge (single-leg if able): 3 sets × 8–15 reps. Pause at top 2 s. Rest 60–90 s.
Finisher/core:
- Side plank: 3 × 30–45 s per side.
- Optional calf raises on step (double or single-leg): 3 × 15–25.

Day 3 — Rest / active recovery
- 20–40 min walking, light mobility, foam rolling.

Day 4 — Upper B (push emphasis)
Warm-up: bandless shoulder warm-up, 2 light sets push-ups.
1) Close-grip push-ups / diamond push-ups: 4 sets × 8–15 reps (use feet elevated for increased difficulty). Rest 60–90 s.
2) One-arm incline push-up progression or archer push-up: 3 sets × 6–10 reps per side. If not possible, do slow eccentrics on one-arm negatives. Rest 90 s.
3) Inverted rows under door/towel or horizontal rows on bar: 4 sets × 8–12 reps. Slow eccentric. Rest 90 s.
4) Biceps curls alternative: Towel curls—loop towel under foot and curl with controlled tempo (if backpack available, curl with it), 3 sets × 8–15. Triceps extension: 3 sets × 8–15 (bodyweight skull crushers using low edge or bench alternative). Rest 60 s.
Finisher/core:
- Plank to push-up: 3 × 8–12 total reps.
- Optional 6–8 min AMRAP of burpees/light cardio for conditioning.

Day 5 — Lower B (posterior chain + strength)
Warm-up: hip hinges, lunges, ankle mobility.
1) Pistol progression or assisted pistol squat to chair: 4 sets × 5–10 reps per leg (use support or slow eccentrics). Rest 90–120 s.
2) Reverse lunge walking in place (split squat emphasis): 3 sets × 10–14 reps per leg (add backpack if available). Rest 90 s.
3) Nordic curl progression (if safe): 3 sets × 4–8 reps — use knees on mat, anchor feet under bed or sturdy object or simulate with eccentric-only glute-ham emphasis by lowering slowly and using hands to push up. If not possible, do single-leg glute ham raises (lower slowly). Rest 120 s.
4) Hip thrust with back elevated on bed (single-leg possible): 3 sets × 8–15 reps. Rest 60–90 s.
Finisher/core:
- Lying windshield wipers or Russian twists: 3 × 12–20 total.
- Farmer-carry alternative: suitcase carry with backpack around the room for 3 rounds of 60 s.

Day 6 — Optional light full-body or mobility
- Light full-body circuit: 3 rounds of 8–12 push-ups, 8–12 squats, 6–10 inverted rows, 30 s plank. Keep intensity low to moderate.
- Or rest/walk.

Day 7 — Rest

Week 2
Keep the same 4-session split but slightly increase density (reduce rest by ~15–30 s) or increase time under tension to maintain stimulus. Alternate some variations to avoid boredom.

Day 8 — Upper A (pull emphasis)
Warm-up.
1) Pull-ups / slow negatives / assisted holds: 4 sets × 3–8 reps or 6–10 negatives. Add 3–5 s isometric hold at top if possible. Rest 90–120 s.
2) Single-arm inverted row/one-arm towel row progression: 3 sets × 6–10 per side. Rest 90 s.
3) Diamond or deficit push-ups (hands on floor, feet elevated or use book under hands to get deeper): 3 sets × 8–15. Rest 60–90 s.
4) Pike push-ups with 2-s pause at bottom: 3 sets × 6–12. Rest 90 s.
Finisher/core:
- Hanging knee raises from pull-up bar (if safe) 3 × 8–15 or lying leg raises 3 × 10–15.

Day 9 — Lower A
Warm-up.
1) Bulgarian split squats (weighted if possible): 4 × 8–12. Rest 90–120 s.
2) Single-leg RDL slow eccentric: 3 × 8–12 per leg. Rest 90 s.
3) Pulse squats or tempo squats: 3 × 12–20 with 3 s eccentric + 1 s pulse. Rest 60–90 s.
4) Single-leg glute bridge: 3 × 8–12. Rest 60–90 s.
Finisher/core:
- Bicycle crunches or plank variations: 3 × 30–45 s.

Day 10 — Rest / light activity

Day 11 — Upper B
Warm-up.
1) Close-grip/archer push-ups: 4 × 8–15. Rest 60–90 s.
2) Inverted rows progressive overload: 4 × 8–12 (vary angle to make harder). Rest 90 s.
3) One-arm push-up progression or slow eccentric one-arm negatives: 3 × 4–8 per side. Rest 90–120 s.
4) Biceps/triceps bodyweight alternatives (towel curls, bench dips on bed edge): 3 × 8–15. Rest 60 s.
Finisher/core:
- Side-to-side plank reach-throughs: 3 × 12–16.

Day 12 — Lower B
Warm-up.
1) Assisted pistol or single-leg squat progression: 4 × 5–10. Rest 90–120 s.
2) Nordic curl progression / Slow glute-ham raise: 3 × 4–8. Rest 120 s.
3) Hip thrust single-leg: 3 × 8–12. Rest 60–90 s.
4) Calf raises single-leg: 3 × 12–20. Rest 60 s.
Finisher/core:
- Farmer carry/hike with backpack: 3 rounds × 60 s.

Day 13 — Optional light full-body or mobility
- Mobility and easy movement. Short circuit 2 rounds of push-ups, rows, squats for blood flow.

Day 14 — Rest

Notes on intensity and set management
- For each exercise aim to finish within 1–3 reps of failure on the last set. Because load is limited, use tempo (3–6 s eccentrics), pauses at sticking points, and unilateral work to ensure high effort.
- For pull-up work: negatives are valuable. Use 4–6 s eccentric and rest 2–3 min between sets if doing very slow negatives.
- Keep a simple log: record sets/reps, perceived difficulty; if everything feels easy, increase difficulty by changing leverages, adding tempo, or adding backpack load.

Nutrition specifics (for maintenance)
- Calories: aim to maintain current weight. Track intake roughly for the 2 weeks; avoid a sustained deficit. If unsure, add ~200–300 kcal above current intake if weight trends downward.
- Protein: 1.8–2.2 g/kg/day (spread across 3–4 meals). This helps preserve lean mass.
- Carbs: moderate around workouts to support glycogen and training intensity.
- Fats: remaining calories from healthy fats.
- Hydration: at least 2.5–3 L/day, more if hot.
- Supplements (optional): whey/plant protein to hit protein targets; creatine monohydrate 3–5 g/day to help preserve strength during short travel periods.

Recovery & sleep
- Aim for consistent sleep timing, 7–9 h/night.
- Short mobility sessions daily (5–10 min) to prevent stiffness from travel.
- Use contrast showers or stretching if needed to reduce soreness.

Safety
- Check door-frame/pull-up bar installation safety. Don’t perform movements that place the bar under lateral loading if it’s not rated. Use feet on floor for rows if towel method is uncertain.
- Avoid aggressive new maximal attempts during travel; focus on near-failure work but not max singles.

Progress checks when back
- On return, plan to resume the gym hypertrophy block with 1–2 lighter sessions in the first week back to re-acclimate if needed, and then resume heavier loading.

If you want, I can:
- Convert this into printable day-by-day sheets.
- Tailor rep ranges and protein targets to the client’s bodyweight (give me her weight).
- Design exact progressions for pull-up or pistol skill depending on her current capabilities.
